::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Internal working document.** This page reviews the `{DATRAS}` R package as prior art to inform IMBUS WP2 design. It is not an IMBUS deliverable and is not intended for external audiences.
:::

## Overview

The `{DATRAS}` R package (Kristensen & Jardim) was developed independently of and prior to the
IMBUS project. It is not an IMBUS deliverable. This page reviews it purely as prior art — to
understand what data checks and transformations were already established, and to inform the
design of WP2 standardisation work and the `{obus}` proof-of-concept package.

`{DATRAS}` provides tools for reading, subsetting, and analysing ICES DATRAS exchange data.
Its core data structure is the `DATRASraw` object — a named list of three data frames
(`CA`, `HH`, `HL`) with a shared `haul.id` factor linking records across tables.

The notes below document the data checks, transformations, and integrity tests performed during
reading and processing in `R/read_datras.R`.

---

## Data ingestion

Data enter via two routes:

- **`getDatrasExchange()`** — downloads directly from the ICES web service using
  `icesDatras::getDATRAS()`.
- **`readICES()` / `readExchange()`** — reads from a flat CSV exchange file (or a `.zip`
  of one).

Both routes pass through the same normalisation pipeline described below.

---

## Normalisation pipeline

### 1. Missing value replacement (`minus9toNA`)

DATRAS uses `−9` as a sentinel for missing values in numeric fields. The function
`minus9toNA()` scans every numeric column in all three tables and replaces exact occurrences
of `−9` (within floating-point tolerance `1e-14`) with `NA`.

```r
is9 <- which(abs(x[[i]][, ii] + 9) < 1e-14)
if (length(is9) > 0) x[[i]][, ii][is9] <- NA
```

::: {.callout-note}
The tolerance test rather than exact equality (`== -9`) guards against floating-point
representation artefacts introduced during CSV parsing.
:::

### 2. Column name harmonisation (`renameDATRAS`)

`renameDATRAS()` applies two normalisations:

1. **Capitalise first letter** of every column name (handles inconsistencies across
   exchange file versions).
2. **Rename a fixed set of legacy columns** to the names expected by the rest of the package:

   | Old name | New name | Note |
   |---|---|---|
   | `ValidAphiaID` | `Valid_Aphia` | reversal of WoRMS naming |
   | `LngtClas` | `LngtClas` (kept) | exchange files occasionally use `LngtClass` |
   | `AgeRings` | `Age` | CA field |
   | `CANoAtLngt` | `NoAtALK` | CA count field |
   | `NoAtLngt` | `NoAtALK` | alternative CA name |

::: {.callout-important}
**Relevance for {obus}/D2.2:** The DATRAS package maps `ValidAphiaID → Valid_Aphia`,
deliberately moving *away* from the WoRMS/ICES standard name. The {obus} package and D2.2
propose `ValidAphiaID` as the canonical name. These two packages are therefore inconsistent on
this column name. See open issue in AGENTS.md.
:::

### 3. `StatRec` / `AreaCode` harmonisation

The ICES rectangle field is named `StatRec` in HH but `AreaCode` in some older CA submissions.
After renaming, if `CA$StatRec` is absent, it is aliased from `CA$AreaCode`:

```r
if (!is.null(d$CA) && is.null(d$CA$StatRec)) d$CA$StatRec <- d$CA$AreaCode
```

---

## Derived variables (`addExtraVariables`)

### 4. Composite haul key (`haul.id`)

A character key is constructed and stored as a factor in all three tables:

```r
haul.id <- factor(paste(Survey, Year, Quarter, Country, Ship, Gear, StNo, HaulNo, sep = ":"))
```

This is the analogue of {obus}'s `.id` field, with `Ship` instead of `Platform` and `StNo`
instead of `StationName`.

### 5. Length class to centimetres (`LngtCm`)

Length classes are converted to centimetres using a lookup on `LngtCode`:

| `LngtCode` | Multiplier (cm) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `.` | 0.1 | 1 mm resolution (e.g. LngtClas 500 → 50.0 cm) |
| `0` | 0.1 | same |
| `1` | 1 | 1 cm resolution |
| `2` | 1 | 1 cm resolution |
| `5` | 1 | 1 cm resolution (5 cm bins, but class = lower bound in cm) |

```r
LngtCm = lookup(LngtCode, LngtCode2cm) * LngtClas
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Mixed `LngtCode` values within a dataset trigger a warning ("Mixed accuracies found").
NA values in `LngtCode` also warn and are assumed to take the maximum (worst) accuracy
present.
:::

### 6. Species name lookup

Scientific names are resolved from two internal lookup tables:

- **`SpeciesTable.csv`** (TSN codes → scientific name): used when `SpecCodeType != "W"`.
- **`WoRMSTable.csv`** (WoRMS AphiaID → `ScientificName_WoRMS`): used when `SpecCodeType == "W"`.

The resulting `Species` column is a factor of scientific names, applied to both HL and CA.

::: {.callout-note}
The WoRMS table is a static file bundled with the package; it does not query the live WoRMS
API and will drift out of date as taxonomy changes.
:::

### 7. Count reconstruction (`Count` in HL)

A key correction: `HLNoAtLngt` as submitted to DATRAS is normalised differently depending on
`DataType`. The package reverses this to recover the **actual count observed in the haul**:

| `DataType` | Interpretation | Correction applied |
|---|---|---|
| `C` | Already standardised to 1 hour | `Count = HLNoAtLngt × (HaulDur / 60) × SubFactor` |
| `R` | Raw (not hour-standardised) | `Count = HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` |
| `S` | Treated as `R` (see note) | `Count = HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` |

```r
multiplier1 <- ifelse(d3$DataType == "C", d3$HaulDur / 60, 1)
multiplier2 <- ifelse(!is.na(d3$SubFactor), d3$SubFactor, 1)
d3$Count <- d3$HLNoAtLngt * multiplier1 * multiplier2
```

::: {.callout-note}
**DataType `S`:** An ICES February 2012 clarification states that `S` submissions at that
time were misinterpreted by data submitters and are functionally identical to `R`. The package
therefore treats `S` as `R`.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
**Relevance for D2.2 / {obus}:** The {obus} equivalent is `dr_add_n_and_cpue()`, which
computes `n_haul = NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` at the individual record level and
additionally produces `n_hour = n_haul / HaulDuration × 60` as an explicit second output.
The two implementations differ in several ways described below.
:::

### Differences between `{DATRAS}` and `{obus}` for DataType `"R"`

Both packages apply the subsampling factor record-by-record, so summed totals per haul agree
under normal conditions. The differences arise in edge cases and in what the functions
produce.

#### NA `SubFactor` / `SubsamplingFactor`

When the subsampling factor is missing, the two packages diverge immediately:

| Field values | DATRAS `Count` | {obus} `n_haul` |
|---|---|---|
| `HLNoAtLngt = 10`, `SubFactor = 2` | `10 × 2 = 20` | `10 × 2 = 20` |
| `HLNoAtLngt = 10`, `SubFactor = NA` | `10 × 1 = 10` | `10 × 1 = 10` |

Both packages substitute 1 for a missing `SubFactor` / `SubsamplingFactor` when
`DataType == "R"`, reflecting the assumption that absence of a subsampling factor implies
the full catch was measured. *(The {obus} package was updated to match this behaviour in
June 2026; prior to that it propagated `NA`.)*

#### DataType `"P"` (pseudocategory sampling)

DataType `"P"` is not in the DATRAS branching logic. It falls through to the same arithmetic
as `"R"` without any acknowledgement:

```r
# DATRAS — "P" not mentioned; multiplier1 = 1 silently
multiplier1 <- ifelse(d3$DataType == "C", d3$HaulDur / 60, 1)
```

```r
# {obus} — "P" listed explicitly
n_haul = case_when(
  DataType == "C" ~ NumberAtLength * SubsamplingFactor * HaulDuration / 60,
  DataType == "R" ~ NumberAtLength * SubsamplingFactor,
  DataType == "P" ~ NumberAtLength * SubsamplingFactor,   # explicit
  DataType == "S" ~ NumberAtLength * SubsamplingFactor,
  DataType == "-9" ~ NA,
  is.na(DataType)  ~ NA,
  TRUE ~ NA
)
```

The computed value is numerically identical for `"P"`, but {obus} makes the intent explicit and
correctly returns `NA` for `"-9"` and unknown DataTypes rather than silently computing a number.

#### Invalid or missing `DataType`

`DataType = "-9"` is a character string and is **not** caught by `minus9toNA()` (which only
processes numeric columns). It therefore survives into the DATRAS count calculation, where
`ifelse(DataType == "C", ...)` evaluates to `FALSE` and `multiplier1 = 1` — a number is
produced rather than flagged as invalid:

| `DataType` | DATRAS `Count` | {obus} `n_haul` |
|---|---|---|
| `"R"` | `HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` |
| `"P"` | `HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` (silent fallthrough) | `NumberAtLength × SubsamplingFactor` |
| `"-9"` | `HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` ← not caught | `NA` |
| `NA` | `HLNoAtLngt × SubFactor` ← not caught | `NA` |

#### `n_hour` not produced by `{DATRAS}`

The DATRAS package produces only `Count` (estimated numbers in the haul). Per-hour CPUE is
left to the user to compute downstream. {obus} makes it a first-class output:

```r
# {obus} always produces both
n_haul = NumberAtLength * SubsamplingFactor          # numbers in haul
n_hour = n_haul / HaulDuration * 60                 # numbers per hour
```

#### Size-stratified subsampling — a note on aggregation

When `SubFactor` varies within a haul × species group (size-stratified subsampling, documented
in D2.2 for GB-SCT and DK under DataType `"P"` and `"R"`), **both packages compute correctly
at the record level**. The risk is not in the per-row multiplication but in any downstream
workflow that assumes a single uniform `SubFactor` per group — for example, extracting
`SubFactor` from the first record and multiplying by a summed `HLNoAtLngt`. Neither package
protects against that misuse, but it is a more common error pattern with the DATRAS
`Count` column (which masks the original `HLNoAtLngt` and `SubFactor` individually) than with
{obus}, where both `NumberAtLength` and `SubsamplingFactor` remain visible.

### 8. Temporal and spatial convenience variables

Added to HH:

| Variable | Derivation |
|---|---|
| `abstime` | `Year + (Month-1)/12 + (Day-1)/365` (decimal year) |
| `timeOfYear` | `(Month-1)/12 + (Day-1)/365` (seasonal position) |
| `TimeShotHour` | `floor(TimeShot/100) + (TimeShot %% 100)/60` (decimal hour) |
| `lon` | alias of `ShootLong` |
| `lat` | alias of `ShootLat` |

### 9. Roundfish area

A static lookup table (`roundfish.csv`) maps ICES rectangle codes (`StatRec`) to North Sea
roundfish area numbers, added as the factor `Roundfish` in HH.

---

## Integrity checks

### 10. Duplicate rows in HH (hard stop)

```r
dups <- duplicated(d2)
if (any(dups)) stop("Duplicated rows found in HH data - data file is corrupt")
```

Any duplicated row in the Haul Header table causes an immediate error. This is the strictest
check in the pipeline.

### 11. Hauls without length records (warning)

After constructing `haul.id`, HH hauls that have no matching HL records are identified and
printed as a warning:

```r
diff <- setdiff(levels(d2$haul.id), levels(d3$haul.id))
if (length(diff) > 0) {
    cat("========= WARNING: ============\n")
    cat("Hauls without length info will be interpreted as empty hauls:\n")
    print(diff)
}
```

These hauls are retained in HH and treated as zero-catch hauls — consistent with the
"zero-station" concept used in `dr_cpue_length()`.

### 12. HL haul level consistency (hard stop)

```r
stopifnot(nlevels(d3$haul.id) == nrow(d2))
```

After alignment, the number of distinct haul levels in HL must equal the number of rows in HH.
Failure would indicate a mismatch between the exchange tables.

### 13. CSV file row-count integrity (`readICES`)

When reading from a flat CSV exchange file, the function counts header lines and data rows and
checks they account for every line in the file:

```r
if (sum(sapply(d, nrow)) + length(i) != length(lines))
    stop("csv file appears to be corrupt.")
```

### 14. Unique haul IDs when combining datasets (`c.DATRASraw`)

When merging two or more `DATRASraw` objects with `c()`, a pre-flight check ensures no `haul.id`
appears in more than one object:

```r
testUniqueHaulID <- function(args) {
    x <- lapply(args, function(x) levels(x$haul.id))
    if (length(unique(unlist(x))) != length(unlist(x)))
        stop("Haul ids must be unique.")
}
```

### 15. Missing haul IDs in CA (`fixMissingHaulIds`)

Older DATRAS CA submissions sometimes omit the full haul key. The package attempts to impute
missing `haul.id` values by fuzzy-matching on (`StatRec`, `Year`, `Quarter`, `Country`, `Ship`).

Two modes controlled by `strict`:

- **`strict = TRUE`** (default): only uniquely matched CA records get a haul ID; ambiguous
  matches are left as `NA` and warned about.
- **`strict = FALSE`**: ambiguous matches receive a randomly chosen candidate haul; a fallback
  on `Roundfish` area is attempted for still-unmatched records.

A warning reports counts: total missing, uniquely matched, randomly assigned, and permanently
unmatched.

---

## Downstream checks in `addSpectrum`

`addSpectrum()` (used to aggregate HL into per-ICES-square length frequency matrices) performs
additional checks:

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Multiple species in HL | Warning ("spectrum will contain all species") |
| `NA` in HH `DataType` | Warning + those hauls removed before spectrum calculation |
| `DataType == "S"` in HL | Warning ("will be interpreted as DataType `R`") |

---

## Summary of checks

| # | Check | Location | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Replace `-9` with `NA` | `minus9toNA` | Transform |
| 2 | Capitalise / rename columns | `renameDATRAS` | Transform |
| 3 | `AreaCode` → `StatRec` in CA | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 4 | Composite `haul.id` constructed | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 5 | `LngtCm` derived; mixed `LngtCode` | `addExtraVariables` | Transform / Warning |
| 6 | Species names from TSN/WoRMS lookup | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 7 | Count corrected for DataType & SubFactor | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 8 | Temporal/spatial convenience fields | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 9 | Roundfish area lookup | `addExtraVariables` | Transform |
| 10 | Duplicated HH rows | `addExtraVariables` | **Error** |
| 11 | Hauls without HL records | `addExtraVariables` | Warning |
| 12 | HL haul level count vs HH rows | `addExtraVariables` | **Error** |
| 13 | CSV row-count integrity | `readICES` | **Error** |
| 14 | Unique haul IDs across combined objects | `c.DATRASraw` | **Error** |
| 15 | Missing CA haul IDs imputed | `fixMissingHaulIds` | Transform / Warning |
| 16 | Multiple species in spectrum | `addSpectrum` | Warning |
| 17 | `NA` DataType in spectrum | `addSpectrum` | Warning + removal |
| 18 | DataType `S` in spectrum | `addSpectrum` | Warning |
